newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait arrests Arab sabotage suspects.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait arrests Arab sabotage suspects.

text.p: Kuwait has arrested a non-Kuwaiti Arab group suspected of planning sabotage against a fellow Gulf Arab state, a security source said on Monday.

The source did not disclose the nationality of the suspects whom it said were detained last Wednesday, but al-Watan newspaper said a "Bahriani cell" of 11 people were arrested for illegally collecting donations and circulating leaflets "abusive of the ruling regime in Bahrain".

The security source told Reuters the suspects intended "to carry out sabotage acts, planned and arranged in Kuwait, to harm the interest of Kuwait and its ties with other Gulf Arab countries. They were discovered before executing them (plans).
"They would have harmed the state security and at the very least would have harmed relations with a fellow Gulf country."
The London-based opposition Bahrain Freedom Movement said on Saturday Kuwait had arrested 11 Bahraini Shi'ite Moslems last week.
Kuwait's Interior Ministry said the arrested group "intended illegal acts that would have harmed the security of Kuwait", the official Kuwait News Agency reported on Sunday night.
Members of Bahrain's majority Shi'ite community have waged sporadic protests, bombings and arson attacks since December 1994 to press for political and economic reforms by the Sunni-led government.
Kuwait, which has a Shi'ite minority of about 30 percent of the some 720,000 Kuwaitis, has long been a firm financial and political backer of Bahrain.
